Solve a Prepared Batch

Source: R/solveODE.R
solveBatch.Rd

Re-solves the conditions of a prepareBatch() handle with new numbers. Only parms, tangent, hessian, cotangent, curvature, adjoint and store may change; anything else needs a fresh handle.

Each of these arguments is a list with one element per condition, matched to the prepared conditions by position; names are ignored. A NULL element keeps that condition's prepared value, and NULL (default) for the whole argument keeps all of them.

Usage

solveBatch(
  handle,
  parms = NULL,
  tangent = NULL,
  hessian = NULL,
  cotangent = NULL,
  curvature = NULL,
  adjoint = NULL,
  store = NULL,
  cores = NULL,
  traceFile = NULL,
  onFailure = c("stop", "warn", "silent")
)

Arguments

handle

A "cppDEbatch" object from prepareBatch().

parms

List of named numeric vectors.

tangent, hessian, cotangent, curvature

Lists of arrays, each as the argument of the same name in solveODE() and of the prepared shape. A cotangent may have another number of seed columns than the prepared one; rows and state columns stay.

adjoint

List of adjointControl() objects.

store

List of checkpoint stores, each the $store of an earlier reverse solve. Here a NULL element integrates that condition afresh.

cores, traceFile, onFailure

As in solveODEBatch().

Value

A list of solveODE() results, named as the prepared conditions.

See also

prepareBatch(), solveODEBatch()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (codegenAvailable()) {
  ## Marshal the conditions once, then re-solve with new numbers, as inside an
  ## optimizer.
  f <- cppODE(c(x = "-k*x"), deriv = FALSE, compile = FALSE)
  r <- cppODE(c(x = "-k*x"), derivMode = "reverse", compile = FALSE)
  compile(f, r, output = "solveBatch_example")
  conditions <- list(a = list(parms = c(x = 1, k = 0.1)),
                     b = list(parms = c(x = 2, k = 0.1)))
  h   <- prepareBatch(f, conditions, times = 0:5)
  res <- solveBatch(h, parms = list(c(x = 1, k = 0.5), c(x = 2, k = 0.5)))
  res$b$variable

  ## Reverse mode: the forward passes keep their checkpoints, and a prepared
  ## sweep reuses them for a new cotangent.
  fw <- solveODEBatch(r, lapply(conditions, c, keepStore = TRUE), times = 0:5)
  W  <- matrix(1, 6, 1, dimnames = list(NULL, "x"))
  hr <- prepareBatch(r, conditions, times = 0:5, cotangent = W)
  solveBatch(hr, cotangent = list(W, 2 * W),
             store = lapply(fw, `[[`, "store"))$b$cotangent
}
# }
